notes: v10.4 BUILD REFRESH (2026-11-21, b4779 — the twenty-second cut — words you said are never merged into one; a spoken word is never called a phantom; prices and spelled letters, notarized): (1) Words you said are never merged into one. The absolute truth rule now also runs as the last step, after every other rule: when two or more real words that were heard have been written as fewer words, the change is undone. This is what turned "sale to" into a Dictionary name. What may still join heard words: numbers, prices and addresses; the same letters with the space removed; your own stutter and filler settings; a name you taught by correcting it repeatedly and said without a pause; a Dictionary entry said exactly; and a join made by the pause rule (words said with no gap between them that sound like one word), which is left exactly as before.
